To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CMB B−mode polarization is a powerful tool to constrain primordial tensor power, and that (2) the inclusion of a DE component in the cosmological model has the effect of reducing the constraining power of CMB B−modes, but this effect can be mitigated by including sub-orbital measurements of the same power.

the presence of DE may affect CMB B−mode measurements of primordial gravitational waves, and that the inclusion of CMB lensing data from sub-orbital observations is crucial in order to restore the expected performances in cosmological models with a non-trivial DE component.

(a) in the presence of DE, a CMB satellite experiment alone will be less sensitive to PGWs than in the case of a cosmological constant; (b) the inclusion of suborbital CMB experiments and/or other cosmological probes allows to restore the constraining power of CMB satellites in the case of non-standard expansion histories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the capability of future CMB experiments in measuring the tensor-to-scalar ratio r, in the presence of a DE component with a non-standard evolution.

the possibility that the expansion history in the epoch relevant for CMB lensing could be different than the ΛCDM model; in particular, we focus on early DE models, in which the Universe is dominated by a DE component already at early times.

the capability of future cosmological observations to constrain the abundance and spectral tilt of PGWs in the presence of a parametrization of DE, showing that the inclusion of the latter may have a significant effect on the constraints on r, and on the detection of the tensor tilt.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in order to fully exploit the potential of the CMB experiments, the combination with other data sets is necessary.
the inclusion of a parametrization for the expansion history does affect the measurement of PGW, but this effect is reduced to a few percents when combining different cosmological probes.

the inclusion of a parametrization of the DE in the analysis of the CMB polarization power spectrum, and in particular of the B−mode polarization power spectrum, does not have a dramatic effect on the constraints on the primordial tensor-to-scalar power ratio, as the effect is partially counterbalanced by the inclusion of other probes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of CMASS and LOWZ BAO data from SDSS-III BOSS, SNe data from Union2.1 and Hubble constant measurement from HST, together with CMB data from Planck satellite, can constrain the abundance and the first derivative of the DE equation of state with respect to the scale factor with a fractional error of the order of 0.2.
, for the purpose of measuring PGWs, the CMB lensed B−mode power spectrum can be considered a standard candle.

, for the parametrization of early Dark Energy that we have chosen, the inclusion of a cosmological expansion history different from the standard one has the effect of reducing the sensitivity of the B-mode measurement to the primordial gravitational wave amplitude, and that this reduction can be compensated by combining CMB data with other cosmological probes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the measurement of PGW from B−mode CMB polarization is robust against uncertainties in the cosmological expansion history, and that the combination of CDM and DE parameters is feasible in future cosmological surveys.

the inclusion of a parametrization for the DE in the analysis of the B−modes power spectrum does not affect the constraining power of CMB experiments on PGWs, provided that sub-orbital measurements are included.

the presence of DE may affect the measurement of PGW in the CMB polarization, and this effect is particularly important in models in which the DE is present in the early universe, as it affects the lensing signal at small scales.
